slides.label: POTL
slides.headline: Freehold, but there's a *monthly fee*? That's a POTL.

slides.label: What it is
slides.headline: A *parcel of tied land*.
slides.body: You own your home and lot outright. A common elements corporation owns and maintains only the shared parts.

slides.label: Typical fee
slides.headline: a month in most new low-rise communities.
slides.body: Shared laneways, visitor parking, snow clearing, insurance and a reserve fund.

slides.label: Before you sign
slides.headline: Get the fee *in writing*.
slides.body: Ask what it covers and whether a reserve fund study has been done. First-year budgets are estimates and tend to rise.

caption:
Told freehold means no fees, then found one in the agreement? That's a POTL.

You own your home and lot. A common elements corporation looks after shared laneways, visitor parking and similar.
Most new low-rise POTL fees run about $75 to $250 a month.
A POTL may also bring a short rescission right, so ask your lawyer early.

slides.headline: Myth: your closing date is *the day you move in*.
slides.body: The first date is tentative and builders can extend it on notice. Tarion delay compensation tops out at $7,500 in total.

caption:
Planning a move around the date in your agreement? Wait until it's firm.

The first closing date is tentative, and builders can set new dates on notice.
Tarion's delay compensation is $150 a day, capped at $7,500, and you must claim within 180 days.
